# World in brief: flight disruptions continue in America; Ukraine warns against Donbas concession

Photograph: Houston Chronicle via Getty Imag

Nov 15th 2026(updated 6h ago)

The head of America’s **Federal Aviation Administration** said that air travel in the country is not expected to return to normal until late on Sunday. Flightaware, an aviation website, said that 1,445 flights scheduled for Sunday had already been cancelled, following 6,696 on Saturday. The flight outage was caused by a contractor upgrading equipment used by air-traffic controllers, leading to a communications failure. That prompted a nationwide ground stop—only the second since the September 11th attacks.

macro_synthesis.headline_zh: 英伟达治理巨震引爆AI重估，中国算力替代与绿能出海迎逆势重定价
macro_synthesis.executive_summary: 本期《经济学人》揭示全球跨市场定价锚正经历三大历史性断裂与重构：第一，美股AI叙事遭遇“治理黑天鹅”与“商业化大考”双杀。黄仁勋因涉华算力走私与私德丑闻闪电辞职并波及美国商务部长卢特尼克，不仅击碎英伟达的“创始人治理溢价”与政商游说缓冲带，更叠加软银NAV暴跌与民主党中期选举后的监管清算，迫使华尔街将定价锚从“通用GPU军备竞赛”强制切换至Anthropic IPO所验证的“企业级Agent真实ARR转化率”与定制化ASIC分流。第二，中国碳排放越过结构性峰值，全面电气化与对东盟绿能科技出口狂飙形成闭环，“经济利己主义”驱动的绿色技术通缩有效对冲欧美关税壁垒，重塑全球能源与电网资本开支长周期。第三，主权资产没收风险回潮、中国国家安全底线思维强化及西方对华认知赤字加深，叠加美国各州公投折射的民生实用主义转向，推动全球资金从美股高集中度科技权重股撤出，向黄金硬资产、美股等权价值股以及中国全栈自主算力、特高压绿电与平价出海消费龙头进行跨市场再平衡。

cross_market_chains.chain_title: 主线一：英伟达治理崩塌与BIS极端鹰派化下的全球算力权力大转移
cross_market_chains.economist_trigger: 黄仁勋因涉华代理人Megaspeed算力走私及私生活丑闻4天内闪电辞职，风暴波及美国商务部长卢特尼克，同时Anthropic推进巨型IPO倒逼AI商业化ROI验证。
cross_market_chains.macro_channel: 关键人治理风险溢价飙升 + 美国国会强制接管BIS出口管制审查 + 华尔街DCF贴现模型从“算力CapEx规模”切换至“B端Agent真实自由现金流转化”。
cross_market_chains.us_mapping: 英伟达（NVDA）与软银系高beta硬件遭遇估值倍数（P/E）压缩与机构持仓上限下调；资金向定制化ASIC（AVGO、MRVL）、第二GPU供应商（AMD）、代工枢纽（TSM）及Anthropic云生态（AMZN）迁移。
cross_market_chains.cn_mapping: 海外高端芯片转口套利空间彻底归零，绑定海外专有生态链标的短期承压；国产AI芯片（海光信息、寒武纪）、晶圆代工（中芯国际）与国产服务器液冷迎来强制性订单替代。
cross_market_chains.divergence_insight: 美股定价核心在于“去单一巨头垄断化”与“防范硬件CapEx周期见顶”，表现为算力内部结构分流与指数去集中化；A股定价核心则是“外部断供极限施压下的生存性替代”，国产算力脱离美股映射走出独立政策与订单驱动行情。

cross_market_chains.chain_title: 主线二：中国碳达峰历史拐点与绿能出海东南亚的“南方增量”重估
cross_market_chains.economist_trigger: 中国碳排放量跨过结构性峰值并加速下降，且中国对东南亚清洁技术（EV、光伏、储能）出口额创历史新高以规避欧盟配额与美方关税壁垒。
cross_market_chains.macro_channel: 中国全产业链规模效应输出70%成本降幅的“绿色技术通缩” + 东盟工业化电力缺口与无本土老牌车企保护主义阻力 + 全球电网消纳瓶颈倒逼储能与特高压CapEx扩张。
cross_market_chains.us_mapping: 传统跨国油气与海运煤炭（XOM、BTU）面临长期远期需求曲线下移折价，美股本土高成本光伏制造受压，而全球铜铝关键金属（FCX）与公用事业级电网改造设备受益。
cross_market_chains.cn_mapping: 东盟市场高毛利增量有效对冲欧美关税折价，中国整车及KD件出海（比亚迪）、大储与逆变器（阳光电源、德业股份）、特高压电网设备（国电南瑞、思源电气）及绿电核电资产迎来估值与EPS双击。
cross_market_chains.divergence_insight: 欧美市场将中国绿能产能视为“产能过剩威胁”并试图以关税筑墙，导致本土能源转型通胀化；中国企业则通过东南亚本地化建厂与电网标准输出开辟“全球南方”第二增长曲线，实现从周期制造向全球能源基建定价者的跃迁。

cross_market_chains.chain_title: 主线三：“掠夺型国家”回潮与国家安全叙事下的战略硬资产重定价
cross_market_chains.economist_trigger: 《经济学人》警示一战式主权与私人海外资产没收重回现代经济战核心，叠加中国首席意识形态智囊高频警示内外部安全威胁、西方驻华记者断代加深跨国信息鸿沟。
cross_market_chains.macro_channel: 国际产权保护公地武器化推升跨境FDI制度成本 + 全球央行去单一法币化 + 外资配置中国资产的股权风险溢价（ERP）结构性分化。
cross_market_chains.us_mapping: 高海外重资产暴露与高中国营收敞口的跨国工业/可选消费股面临估值折价，而黄金矿企（NEM）、国防军工与国家安全情报软件（PLTR、LMT）及跨境合规尽调机构获益。
cross_market_chains.cn_mapping: A股/港股内部“安全资产”对“纯外资审美资产”显著溢价，黄金与战略小金属（紫金矿业、山东黄金）、国防军工与卫星互联网、高股息央国企红利及港股高回购蓝筹成为内外资公约数。
cross_market_chains.divergence_insight: 华尔街因信息鸿沟扩大而对中资民营消费与题材股要求更高的风险补偿（压制P/E上限），但中国本土长线资金与主权基金正围绕“国家安全、资源自主与确定性分红”构建独立于外资审美的本土估值体系。

cross_market_chains.chain_title: 主线四：全球民生降本诉求与中国特许加盟供应链的跨国降维打击
cross_market_chains.economist_trigger: 美国州级公投跨党派支持提高最低工资与限制生活成本，同时中国餐饮零售掀起万店特许加盟革命（杨国福、蜜雪冰城、名创优品）并大举出海。
cross_market_chains.macro_channel: 美国服务业用工成本刚性上升挤压传统餐饮利润率 + 中国“重数字化供应链+轻门店资产”加盟模式输出极致性价比与高ROIC + AI千人千面动态定价优化零售库存效率。

cross_market_chains.divergence_insight: 美股消费板块受困于“顽固服务业工资通胀与中低收入群体购买力挤压”的滞胀式矛盾；中资新消费龙头则将国内商业地产租金下行与供应链通缩转化为“轻资产特许加盟出海”的成本利刃，在全球大众消费降级周期中实现逆势扩张。

岁末年初中国中央经济工作会议定调与全球黄金/铜库存异动（跟踪“国家安全与战略科技自立自强”财政倾斜力度、电网特高压投资批复节奏，以及地缘摩擦下央行购金速率）。

core_articles.title: China’s exports of clean tech to South-East Asia are soaring
core_articles.description: Unlike in the European Union, governments don’t fret about the influx
core_articles.lead_excerpt: I n recent years, China’s green-tech manufacturers have salivated over the market for their stuff in Europe. Demand there has surged as countries and consumers try to reduce their reliance on fossil fuels. European governments are becoming fretful about the impact on their industries and are trying to curb the influx, such as by imposing quotas on electric vehicles. But Chinese firms have options closer to home. Their exports to South-East Asia are soaring. Few in the region whinge.

core_articles.core_thesis: 面对欧盟对华电动车配额及关税围堵，中国清洁技术制造商正加速向东南亚转移，对东盟光伏、储能及EV出口额创历史新高且当地政府鲜有贸易保护阻力；东南亚工业化电力缺口与本土缺乏竞争性老牌车企的制度结构，使中国廉价绿能设备成为东盟降低化石能源依赖与能源转型成本的最优解；跨市场定价层面，东盟需求有效对冲欧美贸易壁垒引发的产能过剩折价，驱动中国光储及出海整车龙头迎来海外EPS上修与P/E估值修复。
transmission_chain: 一阶冲击：欧盟贸易壁垒升温倒逼中国光伏、锂电与电动车企加速向东盟十国倾注产能与绿地投资，东南亚跃升为中国绿能出口核心增量市场。
二阶传导（利率/监管/供应链/CapEx）：东盟各国推行零关税或本土组装补贴政策吸引中企建厂，不仅消化中国国内冗余产能，更带动区域电网改造与充电基建CapEx周期开启。

core_articles.title: The Bottom Line newsletter: Nvidia will never be the same
core_articles.description: Shailesh Chitnis, our chip-industry expert, reflects on the fall of Jensen Huang
core_articles.lead_excerpt:
Billionaires behaving badly is hardly news. Yet the speed of Jensen Huang’s unravelling stands apart. On November 8th Nvidia’s boss confessed to an affair, after reports linked him to an executive at Megaspeed, one of Nvidia’s customers, who is suspected of smuggling chips into China—and working for Chinese intelligence. Three days later came reports of a second affair, with a subordinate. By November 12th the pressure was too much and Mr Huang resigned, ending a 33-year reign in less than a week. (Reports of a third affair have since surfaced.) When I interviewed Mr Huang in June in Taipei, he told me he was good at “seeing around corners”. Evidently not this one.

It would be hard to devise a more thorough act of self-sabotage. His fall is all the worse because he sold himself as different from other tech moguls. On the trip I spent following him around, I discovered he is treated in Taiwan less as a billionaire than as a local boy made good. His wife and parents were often at his side, adding to his wholesome appeal. The Taiwanese have nicknamed him “the People’s Dad”, a man unchanged by success. As I noted at the time, he had projected that image with care.

Mr Huang inspired fierce loyalty inside Nvidia, too. He was a famously tough boss, known for dressing down senior executives in full view of their colleagues, yet staff regarded him as fair. Mistakes were called out but not punished, so long as they were owned up to promptly. A long-serving executive explained to me that no one at Nvidia is allowed to “fail alone”: when something goes wrong, “it can’t be because only one person knew about it, made a decision, then they go cover it up.” Mr Huang, it seems, held himself to a laxer standard.

Small wonder, then, that the employees I spoke to this week sounded disappointed. Before his resignation, one insisted that it was still business as usual, and Mr Huang’s emails to staff read as though nothing had happened. Few at Nvidia were ready for what came next. The company had no public succession plan and its founder had never nominated an heir. Colette Kress, the finance chief now serving as interim boss, could hardly have imagined taking the job a week ago. For the first time in its history, Nvidia faces a future without Mr Huang.

core_articles.lead_excerpt: A t the start of the summer, the outlook was sunny for SoftBank and its swashbuckling boss, Masayoshi Son. The giant investment firm briefly toppled Toyota as Japan’s most valuable company. At the end of June the net value of its assets reached ¥72.3trn ($445bn), an increase of 80% in just three months thanks to gains in its artificial-intelligence holdings. Mr Son crowed that investors had once again underestimated SoftBank (and himself), likening his creation to a goose laying golden eggs: “What matters is not the eggs. It is the goose itself.”

core_articles.title: The return of the snatch-and-grab state
core_articles.description: A new history of confiscation sheds light on modern economic warfare
core_articles.lead_excerpt: A S A QUAKER, A. Mitchell Palmer did not relish conflict. In 1913 the American congressman turned down an offer to serve as secretary of war. But conflict in Europe challenged his pacifism. Six months after America joined the fight against Germany and Austria-Hungary in 1917, Palmer was appointed Alien Property Custodian. The job put him at the forefront of the economic battle against the two aggressors. Tasked with seizing enemy-owned assets across the American economy, his office hoovered up factories, stocks, buildings, patents and more. Soon it began auctioning these to raise money for the war effort. By 1918 Palmer was helping to finance the fighting with the enemies’ own wealth. Germany began the war as the world’s third-biggest foreign investor, after Britain and France. By the time the guns fell silent, more than half of its foreign assets had been confiscated.

A sex-and-spying scandal is rocking Nvidia, the top chipmaker. America’s Democratic Party, having won the midterms, is raring to go after data centres and Trump-adjacent tech titans. Some fear an almighty tech bust is coming. How worried should the world be?

digest_articles.summary_zh: 《经济学人》每周时事讽刺漫画栏目，以幽默笔触描绘英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋在引领全球人工智能算力狂潮的同时，不得不周旋于地缘政治芯片出口管制、反垄断监管审查以及科技巨头自研芯片竞争之间的微妙处境。
digest_articles.market_note: 虽为漫画栏目，但折射出全球市场对英伟达（NVDA）贸易合规与监管风险的高度关注，情绪面映射美股AI算力链及A股国产算力替代逻辑。
